item.title: NVIDIA Earth-2 Introduces AI Data Assimilation for Localized Weather Forecasting
item.description:
NVIDIA Earth-2 Introduces AI Data Assimilation for Localized Weather Forecasting

NVIDIA Earth-2 now includes AI data assimilation tools that allow organizations to process observations more efficiently and incorporate proprietary or third-party data into weather forecasting pipelines.

💡 Why it matters

Weather-sensitive industries use these tools to manage physical risk and improve operational decisions. Capabilities include:

  • Increased Frequency: Issuing forecasts more frequently than fixed-schedule numerical analyses.
  • Real-time Alignment: Keeping estimates aligned with real-time conditions.
  • Localization: Tailoring pipelines to specific regions, such as transmission corridors, production sites, or densely populated areas.
  • Sector Application: Supporting capital markets, insurance, agriculture, logistics, and energy production.

🧩 How it works

Score-Based Data Assimilation (SDA) is used to integrate observations into diffusion-based AI forecasting and downscaling models, such as StormCast and CorrDiff.

  • Consistent Predictions: SDA guides models toward predictions consistent with observations without requiring the model to be retrained.
  • The Denoising Process: Diffusion models generate high-resolution predictions via denoising steps; at each step, SDA compares intermediate predictions with observations to nudge the model.
  • Observation Operators: To nudge the model, an observation operator maps model output to the expected quantity at a measurement location. This can be:
    • Direct: Interpolating nearby grid values for physical quantities like wind speed or temperature.
    • Proxy: Using observed impacts, such as using wind turbine power output as a proxy for wind speed.
  • Probabilistic Output: Results show less uncertainty near observation locations and a wider spread further away, where predictions rely on AI simulations and other model inputs.

⚙️ Key details

  • Performance Factors: The effectiveness of SDA depends on the accuracy, number, and spatial distribution of observations, the quality of the observation operator, and the characteristic length scales of the predicted field.
  • Example Implementation: Using Earth2Studio, a pretrained CorrDiff model for Europe can turn 0.25° weather fields into 2.2-km predictions. In a test case limited to northwestern Germany and part of the Netherlands, 10-meter wind speeds were assimilated using GHCN wind observations and ERA5 data for low-resolution conditioning.

#NVIDIA #Earth-2 #WeatherForecasting #AIDataAssimilation #DiffusionModels

Source: Turn Your Latest Observations Into Timely Weather Decisions With NVIDIA Earth-2 | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: TAISE Framework Repurposes AI Weather Models for Catastrophe Risk Modeling
item.description:
TAISE Framework Repurposes AI Weather Models for Catastrophe Risk Modeling

A new study proposes the TAISE framework, which utilizes AI weather forecasting models to generate extreme weather sequences for catastrophe (CAT) risk modeling.

🧩 How it works

  • Model Repurposing: The framework repurposes AI weather forecasting models to produce coherent extreme weather sequences.
  • Self-Iterative Generation: TAISE uses self-iterative generation to produce continuous global atmospheric fields, allowing extreme events to emerge.

💡 Why it matters

  • Cost Reduction: A proof-of-concept experiment showed an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost compared to conventional methods.
  • Improved Continuity: The framework captures temporal continuity and cross-regional correlations, which are absent in snapshot-based approaches.
  • Modernization: Traditional CAT risk models have relied on costly manual construction for weather scenarios, an approach largely unchanged since the 1990s.

#AI #WeatherForecasting #RiskModeling #TAISE

Source: From Manual Construction to AI-Driven Scenario Emergence: Rethinking Catastrophe Risk Modeling

item.title: Google launches WeatherNext 3 AI weather model
item.description:
Google launches WeatherNext 3 AI weather model

Google has introduced WeatherNext 3, an updated AI weather model designed to improve forecast accuracy, particularly for rain and snowfall, by leveraging real-time satellite observations.

🔍 Overview

  • WeatherNext 3 is Google’s latest AI weather model, succeeding WeatherNext 2.
  • It produces forecasts with higher spatial and temporal resolution, described as five times sharper than its predecessor.
  • The model is now integrated into Google Search, Maps, and Gemini.

🧩 How it works

  • WeatherNext 3 makes predictions based on real-time satellite observations, updating forecasts hourly.
  • It ingests live 1-hour geostationary satellite mosaics alongside historical data.
  • The model uses a Functional Generative Network (FGN) mesh transformer to output dense gridded fields, cyclone tracks, and station-level predictions.
  • Unlike traditional physics-based models, it avoids the time-lag associated with solving complex atmospheric equations.
  • It trains directly on sparse weather station observation data and high-quality precipitation sources, including NASA’s IMERG and Google’s own satellite radar-based reanalysis.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resolution: Forecasts temperature and moisture at up to 5-kilometer resolution, other surface variables at 10 kilometers, and atmospheric variables (e.g., wind speed) at 25 kilometers.
  • Update frequency: Produces a new forecast every hour, compared to WeatherNext 2’s 6-hour intervals.
  • Accuracy: Precipitation forecasts are up to 50% more accurate for predictions at least one day in advance.
  • Coverage: Improves forecasts in regions with fewer ground-based rain gauges, such as parts of Latin America, Africa, and Asia-Pacific.
  • Energy applications: Forecasts wind speed at 100 meters (turbine height) and cloud cover/sun radiation levels to support renewable energy planning.

🚀 Availability

  • WeatherNext 3 is now incorporated into Google Search, Maps, and Gemini.
  • Google has collaborated with the US National Hurricane Center and agencies in Asia to enhance forecasting using its AI models.

💡 Why it matters

  • AI weather models like WeatherNext 3 provide faster and more localized predictions than traditional methods, which rely on supercomputers and have inherent time-lags.
  • The model’s hourly updates and high resolution help predict fast-moving weather systems, such as rain and snow, more effectively.
  • It addresses gaps in forecasting for underserved regions, where traditional models are cost-prohibitive.
  • The model supports renewable energy planning by providing precise wind and solar generation forecasts.

#AI #weatherforecasting #Google #WeatherNext3 #renewableenergy #satellitedata

Source: Google says its AI weather model is getting better Source: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
